transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you saw a problem that wasn't yours to fix, and you fixed it anyway.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: I noticed our onboarding docs were out of date when I joined. New engineers were confused. I spent my second week rewriting the getting-started guide, validated it with two new joiners, and got it merged. My tech lead thanked me.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate on a technical decision.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: We had a disagreement about state management. My colleague wanted Redux and I preferred Zustand. The conversation got heated and my manager stepped in. We used Zustand.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you were wrong about something technical.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: I spent a full quarter building a caching layer before realizing our bottleneck was database query design. I had made an assumption without profiling. After that I now profile before I optimize — always.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: What's a weakness you've had to actively work on?

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: My skip-level told me I interrupt people in technical discussions. I started taking notes during meetings. My manager confirmed three months later the team had noticed a difference.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you had to push back on a direction you disagreed with.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: Engineering was asked to cut a security audit. I mentioned in sprint planning I was uncomfortable. My manager said the business call had been made. I documented my concern in the ADR and moved on.
